messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm prototyping a 'billing braid' concept: emit tiny attribution tokens at ingress (metering spine) and do full stitch in the postprocess stitcher. Thinking about moving more attribution decisions into ingest to reduce tail lat. Thoughts?

ajay: Short answer: ingest-side helps latency, hurts operational flexibility. If we commit to stronger decisions at ingest we increase chance of costly backfills.

sam: Agree with @ajay. Also auditability is the tie-breaker for me. We need a reproducible, verifiable event that can be replayed. If ingest is doing heavy logic we must store provenance snapshots.

maria: Right — goal is: minimize per-token compute on hot path but keep a single source of truth for audits. Proposal: ingest emits an immutable token envelope with minimal fields (tenant, request_id, model_id, fingerprint, sample_flags). Stitcher enriches with cost, routing attribution, and invoice keys.

priya: On fingerprinting: make it deterministic across languages and SDKs. My suggestion: sha256(tenant|request_id|canonical_inputs) -> base64url, truncate to 22 chars. Example: ```fingerprint = b64url(sha256(f"{tenant}:{request_id}:{prefix_hash}"))[:22]``` This avoids depending on arrival ordering.

ajay: A few tradeoffs: 1) storage: token envelopes increase event store size. 2) network: more bytes on ingress. 3) idempotency: clients that retry must not create divergent fingerprints. We'll need a canonicalization policy for inputs.

maria: For storage, what about a compact ledger approach: keep the envelope in a compacted topic keyed by fingerprint (append-only but compaction allowed after reconcile)? That gives fast lookup for audits without storing full raw payloads forever.

sam: Compact ledger sounds promising. But compaction + late-arrivals = tricky. We need a watermarking/reconciliation window and a small tombstone strategy. Operational playbook: if late event arrives outside window, route to backfill pipeline that emits audit-only deltas and triggers billing review.

priya: Also: sample_flags in envelope for quality evals. If we want realtime quality monitors, the stitcher can mark flagged fingerprints and stream them to eval pipeline. Keeps hot path cheap.

ajay: Another operational concern: cross-region routing. If ingest fingerprinting is the primary key for billing, we must ensure canonical fingerprint generation is identical across regions/versions. Version the fingerprint scheme and include scheme_id in the envelope. Failback if unknown scheme.

maria: Good call. Include schema_version and scheme_id. Also include a small proof: e.g., first_20_bytes_of_sha256(original_payload) as quick checksum to detect corruption.

ops-bot: CI:integrations build passed for metering-proto v2 (commit f8a3). :white_check_mark:

sam: For rollouts: canary ingest-side attribution on 5% traffic -> compare stitcher output vs new ingest pre-annotations. If mismatch rate < 0.1% after 24h, promote. Need a replayable diff tool for stitcher outputs.

priya: Backfill/repair plan: keep raw events for 14 days in cold storage. Stitcher can rehydrate and re-stitch to produce audit events. If we compacted the envelope, we still have the key->envelope for majority of cases.

maria: Action items: 1) Priya to write RFC for fingerprint scheme + canonicalization rules (PR by EOD Thu). 2) Ajay to cost estimate storage/network delta for envelope per 1M requests. 3) Sam to draft reconcile/backfill playbook and compaction window proposal. We'll use canary as Sam suggested.

ajay: Quick note on metrics: add a 'stitch_mismatch' counter and a per-tenant mismatch_rate gauge. Important for rollout safety.

maria: Thanks team. If no objections I'll start a prototype branch that emits envelope + scheme_id and wire canary to the stitcher.

priya: +1. I'll start RFC.

sam: +1. Also will add the replay diff tool spec to my doc.
